newsitem.title: ITALY: GOLF-Turner keen to repeat Italian golf win.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-Turner keen to repeat Italian golf win.

text.p: BRESCIA, Italy, April 30 - For a golfer there's no better motivation than returning to the venue of a past triumph.

That's exactly how Kiwi golfer Greg Turner feels heading into the 500,000 stg ($NZ1.19 million) Italian Open, being held on the Gardagolf Club, located close to picturesque Lake Garda in northern Italy.
It's the 54th staging of the Italian Open, with the 34-year-old Turner featured prominently in the tournament's official programme holding aloft the spoils of his 1993 victory.
"It's always nice coming back to Italy because I've had a win and two seconds here," said Turner, who along with Stephen Scahill, will be hoping for further New Zealand success this week.
The Italian Open is only Turner's third event on European soil this year after nearly 10 weeks off. But he feels in good touch and ready to take a full part on the circuit, NZPA reports.
"I was close in Spain last week though finishing 26th wasn't anything special but it was a good solid week for me," he said.
"My game is feeling better just about every day at the moment and everything is progressing well. My swing feels really good and my putting is starting to feel really good."
The course, at 6505 metres and par 72, is new to the Italian Open rota though the course staged the 1993 Kronenberg Open, won by Scotland's Sam Torrance with a four-under-par total of 284.
"I played nine holes yesterday and it's long, and if the weather gets cold and damp, it could be really tough," Turner added.
Heading the field competing in Italy is homegrown favourite Costantino Rocca, plus the US Masters-winning duo of Germany's Bernhard Langer and Spain's Jose Maria Olazabal.
